solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dropped a stock complaint food shop rejected

parts.note: BSE (mad cow disease) is an ailment of livestock, i.e. of stock

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the shop's name is read backwards

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared food

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a long-running complaint about a food shop after it was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DELI into ILED. 'Stock' means farm animals, not shares, so the complaint is the cattle disease BSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face by rope, so abseiled means came down, i.e. dropped.

clue.text: Shop ineffectively as stated every fortnight

indicators.note: something stated is spoken, so these words are said out loud

parts.note: to shop is to buy, and ineffectively means weakly

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone's poor shopping habits, or how often they shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as stated' says BUY WEAKLY is heard rather than spelt, giving the identical-sounding BIWEEKLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Biweekly can mean happening once in each two-week period, a fortnight being two weeks.

clue.text: Awkward Eastern doctor has to tweet under curtain

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the next piece is written below, i.e. after, the curtain

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
an arras is a tapestry wall hanging, used as a curtain (Polonius hides behind one in Hamlet)
a bird's tweet is its song, so to tweet is to sing

explanation.surface: A doctor from the East who has to post on Twitter from behind a curtain: an uncomfortable situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweet' looks like social media but is birdsong. In a down answer 'under' means placed below, i.e. after, the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassing situations cause discomfort and unease, so the word is a close synonym of awkward.

clue.text: Lots of Swiss here walk round university hospital

indicators.note: the walk goes round, i.e. surrounds, the other pieces

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or path one walks along
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: Many Swiss people stroll around the university hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' has the walk surround the other two pieces. San (sanatorium) is a dated word for a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a city in Switzerland, so many Swiss people live there.

clue.text: Split wood: remove to the periphery

indicators.note: the removing word sits on the periphery, i.e. on the outside, with the wood inside it

parts.note: to doff a hat is to take it off, i.e. remove it
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Instructions for woodwork: split the timber and take it out to the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like an instruction to chop the wood but is the definition, slang for leaving. 'to the periphery' puts the removing word outside the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is slang for leave in a hurry, which is what dashing off means.

clue.text: Frank's very dry with a learner

definitions.note: the 's is 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay; frank means bluntly honest

parts.note: brut describes the driest champagne
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is extremely dry company alongside a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning plain-spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal honesty is frankness with no softening, so brutal can mean frank.

clue.text: Opposed to conservationists blocking artificial insemination

indicators.note: the conservationists block, i.e. sit in the middle of, the other abbreviation

parts.note: AI is the usual abbreviation for artificial insemination
the NT (National Trust) is the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservationists obstructing an artificial breeding programme because they disapprove of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' sets the conservationists' initials in the middle of the other abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against, i.e. opposed to.

clue.text: Abridge article about Arabian craft

indicators.note: the article is placed round about the Arabian piece, which ends up written ahead of it

parts.note: to abridge is to shorten, i.e. trim
Ar is a dictionary abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Cut down an article about an Arabian boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads 'about' as the article going round the Arabian abbreviation, but that gives the wrong letter order; here 'about' only places the article after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a three-hulled sailing boat, one kind of craft.

clue.text: Flyer left in drier houses

indicators.note: the drier houses, i.e. holds inside it, the other pieces

parts.note: an airer is a clothes horse for drying laundry

explanation.surface: A laundry clue: a flyer was left inside the clothes drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' puts the two short pieces inside the drier. An airer is a clothes-drying rack.
explanation.definitionFit: An airliner is a passenger aircraft, a flyer in the sense of something that flies.

clue.text: Sailor's beginning with a bucket initially and mop

indicators.note: Sailor's beginning means only the first letter of that word is taken
initially means only the first letter of each of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor starts the day with a bucket and mop to clean the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop for cleaning a ship's deck, and to swab is to mop.

clue.text: Artistic movement wasting time with this case

indicators.note: wasting suggests destroying something's form, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an art movement as a waste of time in this case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' rearranges the letters of TIME and THIS CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aestheticism was the late-19th-century movement of art for art's sake, linked with Oscar Wilde.

clue.text: Pass over most recent turbulence at sea

parts.note: to cross something is to pass over it
current means latest, the most recent

explanation.surface: A sailor passes over the latest rough water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross current flows across the main stream, causing disturbed, turbulent water at sea.

clue.text: Star devouring liqueur? It's a slippery slope

indicators.note: the star devours, i.e. swallows inside it, the drink

parts.note: the sun is a star
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur, here standing for the liqueur

explanation.surface: A celebrity downs a liqueur and warns it's the first step to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devouring' puts the drink inside the star. 'Star' looks like a celebrity but is our sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a snowy slope for skiing, literally slippery; the idiom 'slippery slope' is the joke.

clue.text: Hawker originally flies a recluse across Cape

indicators.note: originally means only the original, first letter is taken
the recluse lies across, i.e. around, the cape

parts.note: a loner is someone who keeps apart, a recluse
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A street hawker first flies a lone person across a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawker' looks like a pedlar but is one who hunts with hawks. 'across' puts C inside LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer trains and flies hawks and falcons, so is a hawker in that sense.

clue.text: Withdraw Home Counties game against good Roma

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: SE (South East) stands for the Home Counties, the counties around London
I spy is a children's guessing game

explanation.surface: An instruction to pull out of a match in the Home Counties against a good side from Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' reverses SE + ISPY + G. 'Roma' looks like the Italian name for Rome but means the Romani people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roma are the Romani people, traditionally (now often offensively) called gypsies.

clue.text: One who's sponsored idol given stick crossing line

parts.note: an idol is a false god

indicators.note: the line crosses, i.e. cuts through, the scolding word

parts.note: to give someone stick is to chide them; chid is an old past participle of chide

explanation.surface: An idol is beaten with a stick across the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside CHID. CHID is an archaic past participle of 'chide', meaning scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Godparents sponsor a child at baptism, promising to oversee its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Waterproof paints with ink ground

parts.note: oils are oil paints

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paints mixed with ground ink to make a water-resistant coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges INK into KIN. 'Waterproof' looks like an adjective but is the noun, the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof coat made of oiled cloth, a waterproof.

clue.text: Essential current books by big revolutionary

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word for big is read backwards

parts.note: large means big

explanation.surface: Present-day books alongside a major rebel are indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns LARGE into EGRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means forming a necessary part of a whole, so essential.

clue.text: Glorify ladies cavorting in middle of audience

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the pair from the middle
middle of means only the central pair of letters is taken
cavorting means jumping about, so the letters of ladies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women prancing about in the middle of a crowd, as if to be worshipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges LADIES into DEALIS, which goes 'in' IE, the centre letters of audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to regard something as perfect, which is to glorify it.

clue.text: Wish to avoid second Republican mass for another one

indicators.note: the second of the two Republican letters is avoided, i.e. left out

parts.note: to require is to want or wish for
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A churchgoer hopes a Republican priest won't say a second mass for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid second Republican' drops the second R of REQUIRE. 'mass for another one' is a cryptic hint that the mass is for someone dead, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A requiem is a Mass said for the soul of a dead person.

clue.text: Tricky meeting involving priest and chapter

indicators.note: the meeting involves, i.e. surrounds, the other pieces

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A difficult meeting that drew in a priest and a chapter of clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts the priest and chapter inside the meeting. Eli is the Old Testament priest, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate situation needs careful handling, so it is tricky.

clue.text: Help to finish a French chicken

indicators.note: the help comes to finish the answer, i.e. after the other pieces

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Help is needed to finish cooking a French chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish' puts AID at the end. 'chicken' looks like the bird but is the slang adjective for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken as slang means cowardly, i.e. scared.

clue.text: Leading European twice acquiring posh rug

indicators.note: the other pieces acquire, i.e. take in, the posh letter

parts.note: top means leading, best
U means upper-class, posh
twice says the abbreviation for European is written a second time

explanation.surface: A top European acquiring a smart rug for the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives a second E for European; 'acquiring' takes the posh letter in. 'rug' is slang for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is slang for a hairpiece, and a toupee is a small wig worn over a bald patch.

clue.text: Embrace German repeatedly downing stein in secret

indicators.note: the stein downs, i.e. knocks out and takes the place of, one embrace
repeatedly means the pair is written twice

parts.note: to hug is to embrace
a stein is a beer mug

explanation.surface: Embracing a German again and again while knocking back beer from a stein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives HUGGERHUGGER; 'downing' has MUG replace the second HUG. 'Downing' looks like drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger is an old term for secrecy, so done hugger-mugger means done covertly, in secret.

clue.text: Present golf foursome approaching second in Wentworth

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: second in means the second letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A golf four-ball arriving at the second hole at Wentworth, a famous English golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Wentworth is a well-known golf club in Surrey, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to give it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spout English with German

parts.note: mit is German for with

explanation.surface: An Englishman holds forth at length with a German.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to pour out or discharge, so it means emit.

clue.text: This writer's wife invested in old money that mustn't be touched

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: an electrically charged thing

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money goes into a fund

parts.note: lire were Italy's currency before the euro
this writer means the setter, I, so this writer's (this writer has) is I've

explanation.surface: A writer's wife has put money into an old currency fund that must be left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts the setter's contraction and wife inside the old Italian money.
explanation.definitionFit: A live wire carries electric current, so it is dangerous and must not be touched.

clue.text: Driver allowed tablets to be hidden in spirit on way back

indicators.note: the other pieces are hidden in, i.e. put inside, the reversed spirit
on the way back means read backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit
let means allowed
E is ecstasy, a tablet, so two tablets are E E

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to smuggle pills inside a bottle of spirits on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' reverses the spirit, giving MUR; 'to be hidden in' puts the other pieces inside it. Tablets are E's, ecstasy pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A muleteer drives mules, so is a driver of animals.
